An interesting chart but I'm not sure as to what the point being made is. The author of the tweet makes no claims as to whether the phenomena is good or bad nor does she attempt to explain it.

If you are actually interested in further explanation about the mathematization of economics, I invite you to read the very recent American Economic Review proceeding article by one of the most well respected, contemporary economists, Paul Romer. A link to his own description of the article can be found here.

IMO it's sophistry. Those who push an agenda (Piketty, et al) love to create tons of fancy charts and graphs which show correlations between ice cream sales and shark attacks, then use underhanded language to suggest causation. I don't like it personally.

I suspect that part of this trend is to do with the advances in econometrics that have been made over the past decade. Typically, people aren't just estimating a simple linear model anymore. Using math to explain economic concepts can be really helpful, so long as it's not used to hide behind sloppy analysis and flawed reasoning.
